role: Find changes that regress latency, throughput, or resource usage at realistic scale.

focus.details: N+1 queries, missing indexes for new query patterns, full scans, unbounded result sets, queries inside loops, missing pagination, chatty round-trips.
Accidental O(n²)+, nested loops over large collections, repeated work that could be hoisted or memoized.
Needless copies, large buffers, unbounded caches/maps, loading whole datasets into memory, leaks that grow over time.
Synchronous I/O on hot paths, missing batching, missing connection pooling/reuse, no timeouts, serial calls that could be parallel.
Lock contention, over-broad critical sections, thread/goroutine explosions.
Missing cache where appropriate, or caching that breaks correctness; poor invalidation.
Work added to code that runs per-request/per-item at high volume.

severity.Blocker: The change causes a latency or resource regression severe enough to degrade the user experience or breach an SLO under normal production load — an N+1 on a primary page, an unbounded query on a table that grows, or a memory leak that will OOM within hours.
severity.Major: Measurable regression under realistic load that won't cause an outage but will show up in monitoring — a missing index on a growing query pattern, synchronous I/O on a moderately hot path, or a cache miss that doubles p99 for a subset of requests.
severity.Minor: Suboptimal but tolerable at current scale — an unnecessary allocation that costs microseconds per call, a missing batch that adds a few round-trips on a low-traffic path, or an O(n²) over a collection that's small today.
severity.Nit: Micro-optimization opportunity with no measurable impact — a slightly more efficient data structure, an unnecessary copy of a small value, or a stylistic preference for const over let in a non-hot path.

method: Identify which changed code runs frequently or over large inputs, and reason about its cost as data grows. Distinguish real regressions from micro-optimizations; only raise micro-issues as Nit.
rationale_instruction: States the cost and scaling behavior — how does this get worse as data/traffic grows.
suggestion_instruction: A concrete improvement, not just 'optimize this'.
